quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. You should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap that is large enough for you to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Wait to proceed until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Make sure no children are crossing before you move.

questions.question: When driving at night, if oncoming headlights are blinding you, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beam.
Flash your lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before entering a gap, check traffic behind and to the side of your vehicle. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about steering a vehicle is true?

options.text: Both hands should be placed on the outside of the steering wheel.
Use one hand only when backing up or operating a vehicle control like wipers or lights.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Use both hands on the steering wheel on opposite sides with thumbs up. Use one hand only when backing or operating a vehicle control.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. Position yourself parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to the edge nearest you.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Split the difference.
Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that matches road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that matches road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Adjust your speed based on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles often go slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign (with an arrow) shows where bicycles cross or ride. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles regularly cross or travel near traffic here.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to be sure it is safe.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes caused by drinking and driving?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving crashes is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: You have a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries and no deaths, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who cross against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against the light. You should give the right-of-way to pedestrians, other vehicles, bicyclists, or anyone already in the intersection before you.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the most common cause of traffic crashes. Distractions make drivers miss important signs and sounds needed to avoid crashes.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may hide hazards even if it looks shallow. Turn around and find another route to your destination.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on any road, or uphill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This helps your vehicle roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the vehicle rolls into the curb.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic lanes on a two-lane road. Any driver may pass when no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Rely only on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Rely only on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot. Check several times before changing lanes. Watch traffic in front of you and in the lane beside you.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green signal.

questions.question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
Entering a highway where there are other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when anything else makes conditions unsafe. Even at the posted speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: Before driving while taking medication, you should:

options.text: Get behind the wheel before the medicine takes effect.
Make several rest stops on your trip.
Learn the side effects and adjust your driving if needed.
Ask another person to ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn the side effects and adjust your driving if needed.
questions.explanation: Many medicines can affect your driving. Know the side effects of any medication you take. Do not drive if the medicine makes it hard to drive safely.

questions.question: You have enough space to return to your lane after passing when:

options.text: The other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe gap between your vehicle and the one you passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long stretches of time.

questions.question: If you are moving with other vehicles across railroad tracks, it is safe to stop on the tracks briefly.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on a road with multiple lanes ends ahead. Drivers in the right lane must merge left.
